key_insight: Robot reliability depends strongly on the robot-use interface: effective designs reduce unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback.
engineering_relevance: Treat action abstraction and interaction design as core engineering choices, not merely wrappers around an embodied model.
method: Introduce RUIBench: 30 manipulation tasks across five suites.
Build RUIKit: 13 interfaces crossing six action abstractions with two interaction forms.
Compare interfaces under shared perception and control in simulation.
evidence_signal: Changing only the interface shifted success rates from 45% to 81% for a frontier agent and from 13% to 47% for a fine-tuned 4B model.
watch_item: Simulation results do not establish real-world reliability, and agents frequently declared success despite observable failures, highlighting the need for task-level verification.
paper_title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
